_doc: Maps each [VISUAL: image src=...] / [VISUAL: diagram src=...] semantic id from script.md to a file under videos/flash-sintering-2/. All 5 diag-* are hand-coded SVG block diagrams. All 44 img-* are stylized SVG illustrations using the dark-navy + 3b1b palette (#0e1117 bg, #58a6ff/#ffd866/#ff8c42/#7ee787/#f97583 accents). Stylized illustrations were chosen over web photos because (a) the script needs a dignified, consistent visual register on academic content, (b) license verification for personal portraits and SEM micrographs is unreliable at scale, and (c) consistent illustration matches the 3b1b reference style. No paper-md-assets were re-used because they are journal figures (Hewitt, Lacey, Todd 2017 — copyrighted journal artwork) and the scenes that needed those figures are emitted as [MANIM: ...] cues in script.md (handled by the visualizer).

img-ceramic-powders-sem.method: hand-coded SVG (1920×1080), SEM-style scattering of irregular sub-micron grains + pores, dark-navy bg, scale bar '1 µm'
img-ceramic-powders-sem.description: Stylized SEM micrograph of ceramic powder — the starting point of every ceramic.

img-ceramic-green-body.method: hand-coded SVG. Pressed grey disc (oblique view) with surface pock-marks indicating porosity, callouts: '~60% theoretical density' and 'fragile — crumbles under finger'.

img-sintering-furnace.method: hand-coded SVG. Industrial furnace box with circular hatch glowing orange, model label 'TF-1700', digital readout '1450 °C', vent stacks with shimmer.

img-spark-plug-cutaway.method: hand-coded SVG cutaway of a spark plug — terminal nut, white sintered alumina insulator (highlighted), hex shell, threaded body, gap. Annotations identify the ceramic insulator as sintered Al₂O₃.
img-spark-plug-cutaway.description: Spark plug cutaway showing the white sintered ceramic insulator.

img-dental-crown.method: hand-coded SVG of a tooth-shaped CAD/CAM zirconia crown (off-white tooth silhouette with shading and cusp lines) plus annotation 'milled, then sintered 1500 °C / 2 h'.
img-dental-crown.description: Dental crown — modern CAD/CAM zirconia, sintered.

img-brake-disc-ceramic.method: hand-coded SVG carbon-ceramic brake disc face-on, drilled holes around the rim, hub bolts, abstract red caliper to the side.
img-brake-disc-ceramic.description: Carbon-ceramic SiC brake disc, densified via reactive sintering.

img-soft-substrate.method: hand-coded SVG. White sintered ceramic substrate (oblique view) carrying gold-line traces and a dark SoC chip in the center. Annotation: '99% dense alumina, sintered at 1600 °C, ground flat to ±1 µm'.
img-soft-substrate.description: Microchip mounted on a sintered ceramic substrate — 'every microchip in the room'.

img-tunnel-kiln-industrial.method: hand-coded SVG. Receding tunnel kiln in perspective, inner glow oranging from edges to bright yellow core, vent stacks with smoke. Caption: '~24 h dwell · 1400–1700 °C peak · MW-scale draw'.
img-tunnel-kiln-industrial.description: Industrial tunnel kiln — continuous high-temperature sintering.

img-ceramic-microstructure-sem.method: hand-coded SVG mosaic of polygonal grains (post-sintering microstructure), residual triple-junction pores, scale bar '5 µm'.
img-ceramic-microstructure-sem.description: Sintered ceramic microstructure — large grains result from slow heating.

img-rishi-raj-portrait.method: hand-coded SVG stylized portrait card (silhouette in dark-navy frame with bio block on right) — pioneer of flash sintering, CU Boulder. The official photo is at https://www.colorado.edu/mechanical/rishi-raj but no Wikimedia/CC photo of Raj is available, so a stylized card is used instead.
img-rishi-raj-portrait.description: Rishi Raj — pioneer of flash sintering, U. of Colorado Boulder. Stylized portrait.

img-cu-boulder-engineering.method: hand-coded SVG. Three sandstone-coloured (Boulder's iconic red-tile + sandstone) buildings against a starry mountain skyline.
img-cu-boulder-engineering.description: University of Colorado Boulder engineering complex — stylized.

img-rishi-raj-lab.method: hand-coded SVG. Stylized lab bench: tube furnace (orange glow) on the left, DAQ box with mini current trace in the middle, Sorensen DC supply (V/I displays + knobs) on the right, all wired together.
img-rishi-raj-lab.description: Stylized lab rig — small tube furnace, DC supply, DAQ box.

img-marco-cologna.method: hand-coded SVG portrait card (orange-accent border) with bio: 'PhD student, U. of Trento → CU Boulder ; first author Cologna, Rashkova, Raj 2010 ; now at JRC Karlsruhe'. No public CC photo of Cologna found.
img-marco-cologna.description: Marco Cologna — first author on the 2010 paper. Stylized portrait.

img-boriana-rashkova.method: hand-coded SVG portrait card (yellow-accent border) with bio block: 'Postdoc, CU Boulder ; co-author 2010 ; now at Montanuniversität Leoben'.
img-boriana-rashkova.description: Boriana Rashkova — postdoctoral co-author on the 2010 paper. Stylized portrait.

img-zirconia-disc-electrodes.method: hand-coded SVG. 3D-look ZrO₂ disc with two thin platinum electrode plates top/bottom, dimensions annotated (~3 mm thick, 10 mm dia.).
img-zirconia-disc-electrodes.description: Yttria-stabilized zirconia disc with platinum electrodes — the standard flash-sintering specimen.

img-power-supply-knob.method: hand-coded SVG. Sorensen DLM faceplate: two 7-segment displays (120.0 V, 0.85 A) and a large rotary voltage-coarse knob with orange indicator. Beat caption: 'they pushed it higher than usual'.
img-power-supply-knob.description: DC power supply faceplate — the moment before the first flash.

img-cologna-2010-current-spike.source: generated, after Cologna, Rashkova & Raj, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 93[11] (2010)
img-cologna-2010-current-spike.method: hand-coded SVG re-creation of the canonical four-lane time series (current log-spike, voltage drop as control flips, density jump from 60→99%, power dissipation peak) with shared time axis and a vertical 'FLASH' marker. Not the original journal figure (which would be copyright); a clean, palette-matched re-draw of the same shape.
img-cologna-2010-current-spike.description: Re-creation of the Cologna 2010 current/voltage/density/power vs time trace — the iconic flash-sintering signature.

img-flash-sintered-sample-glow.method: hand-coded SVG. Inside a dark furnace cavity: a glowing white-hot disc between platinum electrodes (radial halo of orange/yellow), wires leaving above and below. Annotations: '~2000 K core' and 'disc shrinks ~20% in <5 s'.
img-flash-sintered-sample-glow.description: Flash-sintered sample mid-event — disc glowing white-hot inside the furnace.

img-conference-room.method: hand-coded SVG. Stylized conference room: ceiling lights, projection screen showing 'FLASH-SINTERING OF YSZ — Cologna, Rashkova, Raj JACS 2010', presenter silhouette by the screen, two rows of inattentive audience silhouettes (some on phones).
img-conference-room.description: Stylized conference scene — 'For about a year, the result was greeted with polite silence.'

img-sglavo-biesuz.method: hand-coded SVG. Two side-by-side stylized portrait cards (blue + yellow accents) labeled 'Vincenzo Sglavo' and 'Mattia Biesuz', U. of Trento.
img-sglavo-biesuz.description: Sglavo & Biesuz (Trento) — first independent reproduction of flash sintering. Stylized portraits.

img-snowball-rolling.method: hand-coded SVG. Night-sky snowy hill with a sequence of progressively larger snowballs (and thicker snow trail) rolling downhill. Annotation: 'In flash sintering, the ceramic IS the hill, AND the snow.'
img-snowball-rolling.description: Snowball-rolling-downhill metaphor for positive feedback / thermal runaway.

img-oxford-mathematical-institute.method: hand-coded SVG. Stylized facade of the Andrew Wiles Building (Oxford Mathematical Institute) — Penrose-tile-inspired diamond pattern on the upper facade, glass strip below. Caption: 'Where Hewitt and Lacey did the analysis (2015)'.
img-oxford-mathematical-institute.description: Oxford Mathematical Institute (Andrew Wiles Building) — home of the Hewitt-Lacey-Todd analysis.

img-richard-todd-oxford.method: hand-coded SVG portrait card (blue-accent border) with bio: 'Emeritus Prof., Oxford Materials ; 2025– President, ECerS ; Joule-only camp, pyrometry advocate'. Official photo at materials.ox.ac.uk/peoplepages/todd.
img-richard-todd-oxford.description: Richard Todd (Oxford) — Joule-only-camp leader. Stylized portrait.

img-raj-press-photo-cu.method: hand-coded SVG portrait card (orange-accent border) framing Rishi Raj as the leader of the defect / electrochemical camp; bio bullets: 'Frenkel-pair avalanche', 'T_blackbody too low', 'atoms hop because there is somewhere to go'.
img-raj-press-photo-cu.description: Rishi Raj — defect / electrochemistry camp. Stylized portrait card.

img-electrochemical-cell.method: hand-coded SVG. Stylized electrochemical cell — anode (+) and cathode (−) flanking a YSZ block, O²⁻ ions migrating to the anode, a darkened reduced layer at the cathode (label 'Zr⁴⁺ → Zr³⁺ → Zr⁰'), battery + wires below.
img-electrochemical-cell.description: Localized cathode reduction — chemistry that pure Joule heating cannot do.

img-flashed-sample-color-difference.method: hand-coded SVG. Two discs side-by-side, one grey (sintered in air), one black (sintered in argon), 'vs' between them. Caption: 'A pure thermal model says: same heat → same outcome. Reality disagrees.'
img-flashed-sample-color-difference.description: Color-change evidence: same powder, same density, different colors depending on atmosphere.

img-periodic-table-ceramics.method: hand-coded SVG mini-periodic-table grid; cells highlighted in orange when the element's oxide flashes (Ti, Mn, Co, Zn, Sr, Zr, Ce); Al highlighted yellow as 'refuses'.
img-periodic-table-ceramics.description: Periodic-table view of which elements' oxides flash and which refuse.

img-zirconia-microstructure.method: hand-coded SVG. Left: YSZ disc photo-style (grey-white). Right: hex-tile micrograph view, scale bar '2 µm', label '3 mol% Y₂O₃ in ZrO₂'.
img-zirconia-microstructure.description: Yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) — the original flash material.

img-titania-sample.method: hand-coded SVG. Powder jar (left) + flash-sintered TiO₂ disc (right), bandgap and activation-energy footnote.

img-strontium-titanate.method: hand-coded SVG. Perovskite unit cell (Sr corners, Ti centre, O face-centred), with isometric projection and colour legend.

img-zinc-oxide-powder.method: hand-coded SVG. Pile of white ZnO powder with grain texture and shading, footnote 'wurtzite, n-type semiconductor, varistor material'.
img-zinc-oxide-powder.description: ZnO — zinc oxide, varistor material. Flashes near 600 °C.

img-ceria-disc.method: hand-coded SVG. Pale-yellow CeO₂ disc with subtle highlight; footnote about fluorite structure and Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺ redox.
img-ceria-disc.description: CeO₂ — ceria, fuel-cell electrolyte. Flashes around 500 °C.

img-mnco2o4-spinel.method: hand-coded SVG. Dark-blue spinel disc (left) plus a thermometer (right) showing other materials' flash temperatures with MnCo₂O₄ at 325 °C highlighted in orange.
img-mnco2o4-spinel.description: MnCo₂O₄ spinel — flashes at 325 °C, the lowest-temperature flash known.

img-alumina-disc-unflashed.method: hand-coded SVG. Pure white Al₂O₃ disc + small inset chart showing nearly-flat log-σ-vs-1/T for Al₂O₃ (red) versus steep YSZ curve (blue dashed).
img-alumina-disc-unflashed.description: Al₂O₃ — alumina. Refuses to flash because its Arrhenius curve is flat.

img-conductivity-curves-comparison.method: hand-coded SVG Arrhenius plot (log σ vs 1/T) with steep flash candidates (YSZ, CeO₂, SrTiO₃, MnCo₂O₄) and flat refusers (Al₂O₃, SiC, WC).
img-conductivity-curves-comparison.description: Side-by-side Arrhenius conductivity curves — flash candidates vs refusers.

img-spark-plasma-sintering-machine.method: hand-coded SVG SPS rig: vertical press frame, top and bottom rams, graphite die in the centre with a glowing core, side electrode cables, pulse waveform indicator, pressure arrow at top.
img-spark-plasma-sintering-machine.description: Spark Plasma Sintering machine — graphite die + uniaxial press + pulsed DC.

img-olevsky-maniere.method: hand-coded SVG. Two stylized portrait cards (green + blue accents) labeled 'Eugene Olevsky (San Diego State)' and 'Charles Manière (U. of Caen)'.
img-olevsky-maniere.description: Olevsky & Manière — Flash-SPS pioneers (2017). Stylized portraits.

img-industrial-furnace-night.method: hand-coded SVG night-time industrial scene: factory silhouettes against deep navy sky, multiple chimneys with smoke and steam, rows of orange-glowing windows, soft atmospheric glow.
img-industrial-furnace-night.description: Industrial ceramics plant at night — energy hungry.

img-sofc-stack.method: hand-coded isometric SVG of a 6-layer SOFC stack (alternating YSZ-electrolyte and Ni-YSZ/LSCF-electrode layers) with side legend and gas-flow annotations (H₂ ⟶, ⟵ O₂, e⁻ → load).
img-sofc-stack.description: Solid oxide fuel cell stack — multiple sintered-electrolyte layers.

img-solid-oxide-fuel-cell-thin-film.method: hand-coded SVG cross-section: porous LSCF cathode (top), dense thin YSZ electrolyte (middle, ≈5 µm, labeled DENSE), porous Ni-YSZ anode (bottom), O²⁻ arrow crossing the electrolyte.
img-solid-oxide-fuel-cell-thin-film.description: SOFC thin-film electrolyte cross-section — dense, fine-grained.

img-battery-cathode-sem.method: hand-coded SVG SEM-style mosaic of spherical secondary cathode particles with subtle texture and primary-particle hints, scale bar '10 µm'.
img-battery-cathode-sem.description: Battery cathode SEM — dense Li-ion conductor secondary particles.

img-3d-printed-ceramic.method: hand-coded isometric SVG of a printed ceramic lattice cube (open-cell square pattern) — fragile-looking, complex geometry.
img-3d-printed-ceramic.description: 3D-printed ceramic part — fragile, porous, distorts in conventional kilns.

img-lucideon-pilot-line.method: hand-coded SVG of a continuous flash-sintering pilot line: conveyor belt with discs moving through an orange-glowing flash chamber containing two electrodes; before-discs grey, post-flash discs lighter; '~5 s/disc' direction arrow.
img-lucideon-pilot-line.description: Pilot-scale flash-sintering line — Lucideon (UK) and NIMS (Japan) demonstrators.

img-cologna-zirconia-sample.method: hand-coded SVG. The original Cologna 2010 YSZ disc on a museum-style pedestal with gold-tinted electrode marks and a small label plaque ('M. Cologna 2010 — YSZ disc · CU Boulder').
img-cologna-zirconia-sample.description: Stylized portrait of the canonical 2010 sample — the disc that started a field.

diag-conventional-vs-flash-sintering.method: hand-coded SVG, two side-by-side panels. Left: conventional kiln with multiple grey discs and large heating waves; stats '1400–1700 °C / hours / MWh per batch' and big '~10 h' callout. Right: small furnace with one glowing disc between electrodes; stats '600–900 °C / seconds / ~10× less energy' and big '~5 s' callout.
diag-conventional-vs-flash-sintering.description: Side-by-side comparison: conventional sintering vs flash sintering.

diag-electric-circuit-setup.method: hand-coded SVG. Tube furnace cross-section with heating coils, 3D YSZ disc between Pt electrodes inside, wires routing up over the top to a Sorensen DC supply box (V = 120 V, I-limit ≈ 1 A/cm²) on the right via an inline ammeter at the top.
diag-electric-circuit-setup.description: Circuit diagram of the flash-sintering setup.

diag-thermal-runaway-feedback-loop.method: hand-coded SVG circular feedback diagram. Five labeled nodes around a dashed ring (1. Voltage applied, 2. Current flows I=σV/L, 3. Joule heating P=I²R, 4. T rises, 5. σ(T) rises) with directed arrows connecting them; central red 'RUNAWAY' label.
diag-thermal-runaway-feedback-loop.description: The thermal-runaway positive-feedback loop — five steps in a closed cycle.

diag-mechanism-comparison.method: hand-coded SVG. Two panels (Joule-only camp vs Defect/electrochemical camp) with Claim/Evidence/Achilles-heel sections each, listing the principal authors (Todd, Hewitt, Dong, Chen vs Raj, Naik, Cologna, Sglavo, Biesuz) and their key arguments.
diag-mechanism-comparison.description: The mechanism war — side-by-side comparison of the Joule and defect camps.

diag-grain-boundary-defects.method: hand-coded SVG. Three large polygonal grains with explicit lattice-dot grids, vacancy rings (red) and interstitial dots (yellow) shown as Frenkel pairs (orange dashed connections); horizontal E-field arrow along the top; legend bar at the bottom.
diag-grain-boundary-defects.description: Frenkel-pair avalanches at grain boundaries — Raj's defect mechanism.
